messages:
Priya (Design): Quick question for the group  leaning toward a compact validation approach for the Console forms. Idea: defer a top summary until submit, but show single-line inline hints/errors only on blur or submit. Keeps the form light while typing. Thoughts?

Tom (Frontend): I like lighter UI when typing, especially on mobile. My worry: users scanning quickly might not notice missing required fields if there's no persistent marker.

Priya (Design): For persistent signposting we could use a subtle suffix in the label e.g. "API key (required)" that is visible but low-contrast. No bright asterisks everywhere.

Li (Engineering): Implementation note: prefer validate-on-blur + validate-on-submit. Avoid validating on every keystroke to reduce noise and validation churn. Simple debounce approach: ```js
let t; input.addEventListener('input', ()=>{ clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(()=>validate(input), 400);});```
This keeps UX responsive without immediate error flashing.

Mara (a11y): A few accessibility points: 1) Required must be programmatically detectable (aria-required). 2) Use aria-live="polite" for inline errors so screen readers get updates but typing isn't interrupted. 3) When showing a top summary on submit, give it role="alert" only on submit so it's read immediately.

Ravi (PM): Also think about destructive confirmations here. We have multiple cases: 1) delete model (prod) 2) remove dataset (non-prod) 3) purge cache. Can we standardize? We keep getting support tickets for accidental deletes.

Priya (Design): Proposal: three tiers: safe (soft delete with undo toast), moderate (checkbox "I understand" + modal), high-risk (typed-confirm with exact name). For high-risk add an explicit delay before enabling final button (e.g., 600ms) to avoid accidental double-clicks.

Tom (Frontend): For typed-confirm: auto-focus the input, disable paste (onpaste="return false"), and show a small inline hint showing exact string to type. Also capture analytics for mistakes so we can tune copy.

Li (Engineering): Agree. For soft delete, make the backend support a recover window (30 days) and expose an API flag "hard_delete=true" only for admin flows. That reduces UX friction but protects data.

Mara (a11y): Accessibility for the modals: trap focus, announce purpose and the risk level, and ensure the confirm input is labelled properly. If we disable the primary button visually, don't rely on color alone; add `aria-disabled` and visible affordance.

Priya (Design): Microcopy callout: instead of "Are you sure?" use explicit cause-and-effect e.g., "Deleting this model will remove all associated versions and cannot be undone." Short, factual, action-oriented. Also companion link to docs for recovery policy.

Ravi (PM): Can we run a small experiment? Roll the compact validation UI to 5% for one week, measure drop in form completion errors and support tickets. For deletes, measure accidental-confirm events pre/post typed confirm.

Tom (Frontend): +1. Also add a quick unit-test checklist for front-end: keyboard-only flow, SR announce on submit, mobile layout. I'll draft test cases.

Priya (Design): I'll drop two mock variations in Figma: A) compact labels + blur-errors + summary-on-submit, B) persistent label markers + inline realtime errors (soft). Will annotate accessibility hooks.

ci-bot: Preview deployed: feature/compact-validation -> https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/forms-compact at 1717004525 :rocket:

Mara (a11y): One more: when summary appears at top after submit, include a link that jumps to the first invalid field (use anchor focus) so keyboard users can quickly fix the first error.

Priya (Design): Great call. I'll include the "jump to first error" behaviour in the mocks and wireframe. Thanks team, will ping when mocks and test sheet are up. :raised_hands:
